questions.question_text_en: Two point charges $+4\,\mu C$ and $+9\,\mu C$ are placed $10\,cm$ apart in air. The distance from the $+4\,\mu C$ charge at which the electric field intensity is zero is:
questions.explanation_en: At the null point, $\frac{k \cdot 4}{x^2} = \frac{k \cdot 9}{(10 - x)^2}$, so $\frac{2}{x} = \frac{3}{10 - x}$, giving $x = 4\,cm$ from the $+4\,\mu C$ charge.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question_text_en: A convex lens of focal length $20\,cm$ forms a real image at a distance of $60\,cm$ from the lens. The object distance is:
questions.explanation_en: Using $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u}$ with $f = +20\,cm$ and $v = +60\,cm$: $\frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{60} - \frac{1}{20} = -\frac{1}{30}$, so the object is at $30\,cm$ from the lens.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.question_text_en: The number of $\sigma$ bonds present in an ethyne ($C_2H_2$) molecule is:
questions.explanation_en: Ethyne has two $C-H$ $\sigma$ bonds and one $C-C$ $\sigma$ bond (the triple bond consists of $1\sigma + 2\pi$ bonds), so there are $3$ $\sigma$ bonds in total.
questions.subject: Chemistry
